description: > We are a team passionate about space and wearable technology. Our project is a smart system to monitor astronaut health like heart rate and oxygen offline. We built a web dashboard using HTML, CSS, JavaScript and Firebase. We are looking for team members interested in AI and design to join us.
summary: WANAS (Wearable Autonomous Neural Analytics System) is an advanced 3-in-1 astronaut health monitoring and support ecosystem created for the NASA Space Apps Challenge. Designed for deep-space and Mars missions, it integrates an AR helmet with intuitive color-coded status displays, a smart vest powered by offline TinyML (<0.1s response), and modular EMS massage units to combat muscle and bone atrophy. Weighing only 1,570g, the system solves critical space challenges—including zero-G noise, motion artifact filtering, and kinetic energy harvesting. Furthermore, its onboard AI Companion provides medical triage, SOS automation, and psychological support against isolation.
details:
. What Does It Do and How Does It Work?

WANAS is a unified, 3-in-1 wearable ecosystem designed to monitor, protect, and assist astronauts in space. It operates through three core modules communicating via Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE):

  • AR Helmet: Features an OLED 4K display and a $360^\circ$ light ring for peripheral vision. Instead of hard-to-read numbers, it communicates status instantly using intuitive colors (Green, Yellow, Red). It weighs 280g and has a 48-hour offline battery life.
  • Smart Vest: Acts as the main AI brain and sensor hub. It tracks vital signs every second—including ECG (e.g., 78 BPM), SpO2 (97%), CO2 levels (0.62%), and body temperature ($36.6^\circ\text{C}$). It uses offline TinyML to process data in under 0.1 seconds.
  • EMS Massage Modules: Comprises 7 modular air-mesh pieces with magnetic quick-locks delivering 10–50 Hz Electrical Muscle Stimulation (EMS). Used for 15 minutes a day, it combats muscle atrophy (which causes a 20% muscle loss in 2 weeks) and bone density decline.

The Operational Flow:

  1. Detect: Sensors capture vital signs and environmental metrics.
  2. Analyze: TinyML processes the data locally offline in $<0.1$ seconds.
  3. Alert: Triggers immediate vibration and a $360^\circ$ light ring alert if danger is detected.
  4. Chat & Prevent: The AI companion answers via voice, and the EMS module automatically initiates preventive therapy.

## 2. What Benefits Does It Have?

  • Ultra-Lightweight & Unified: Weighs a total of just 1,570g (compared to bulky 10kg+ traditional setups) and fits seamlessly inside standard NASA and SpaceX suits.
  • Offline Autonomy: Operates entirely offline with a response time of under 0.1 seconds, eliminating reliance on delayed Earth-to-space internet links.
  • Zero-G Noise & Visual Optimization: Replaces hard-to-read numeric screens with clear color cues, solving the problem of unreadable text in noisy ($70\text{ dB}$) zero-gravity environments.
  • Continuous Power Generation: Incorporates kinetic joint modules that convert astronaut movement into 15–20W of power to supplement battery life.
  • Holistic Health & Psychological Support: Features an AI Companion ("Heart") that assists with medical triage, first-aid, daily psychological check-ins (PHQ-9), storytelling, jokes, and meditation.

## 3. What Is the Intended Impact of the Project?

  • Mission Readiness for Mars 2028: Aimed at deep-space and Mars exploration missions where rescue or immediate medical evacuation is impossible.
  • Mitigating Space Degeneration: Preventing critical space health hazards such as muscle and bone atrophy, back pain (which affects 80% of astronauts), blood clots, CO2 buildup, and radiation risks.
  • Acting as an Autonomous Space Doctor: Providing real-time emergency triage, automated SOS signals with full vitals and GPS coordinates, and psychological stabilization to combat extreme astronaut isolation.

## 4. What Tools, Coding Languages, Hardware, or Software Were Used?

  • Software & Web Platform: Hosted and presented via a dedicated web app (wanas-team.vercel.app).
  • AI & Processing: Edge computing powered by TinyML for real-time offline machine learning analysis.
  • Connectivity: BLE (Bluetooth Low Energy) for wireless synchronization between the helmet, vest, and EMS modules.
  • Hardware Components: OLED 4K displays, ECG/SpO2/CO2/temperature sensors, 7 modular EMS air-mesh pads with magnetic locks, kinetic joint energy harvesters, and Boa Dial automatic fit adjusters.
  • Design & 3D Modeling: Specialized 3D design tools and modeling software to build interactive representations of the smartwatch, belt, helmet, and suit integrations [Memory].

## 5. How Is Your Project Creative?

  • Color-Only Visual Language: Eliminates the cognitive overload of reading numbers in zero-G by boiling status down to a glanceable $360^\circ$ color ring (Green/Yellow/Red).
  • 3-in-1 Modular Integration: Seamlessly bridges life support, health diagnostics, and physical therapy into a single lightweight suit attachment rather than disconnected, bulky equipment.
  • AI Companion with Emotional Intelligence: Combines physiological monitoring with psychological care—providing daily PHQ-9 mental health tracking, stories, and meditation to alleviate space isolation.
  • Self-Sustaining & Adaptive Engineering: Features self-healing outer covers, kinetic power harvesting from joint movement, and sweat-filtering algorithms that prevent false alarms caused by body motion.

## 6. What Factors Did the Team Consider?

  • Environmental & Physical Constraints: Addressed microgravity motion artifacts (which cause standard sensors to produce up to 30% erroneous readings during movement), high background cabin noise ($70\text{ dB}$), radiation exposure, and facial CO2 accumulation.
  • Ergonomics & Comfort: Designed for seamless wear inside spacesuits using breathable Air-Mesh fabrics, automatic Boa Dial sizing, and lightweight components to prevent fatigue.
  • Data Privacy & Security: Ensured strict medical confidentiality by restricting detailed health analytics solely to the astronaut and their flight surgeon, while displaying simple color indicators to the rest of the crew.
  • Operational Reliability: Engineered robust offline fallback systems, automated SOS protocols with satellite uplinks, and energy-efficient power management.
